newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight dips to 7.5 pct vs 8.6/7 on maturity.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight dips to 7.5 pct vs 8.6/7 on maturity.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell to 7.5 percent against 8.6/7 percent on Friday as liquidity improved due to the maturity of a central bank deposit, dealers said on Monday.
They said the overnight fell to 7.3 percent immediately after opening in the afternoon before rising back to around 7.5 to 7.7 percent range.
"Once other interbank rates fell, the overnight was bound to fall," said the dealer with a Malaysian bank.
"It (the overnight) should stay around here," he added.
Other interbank rates fell across the board as many large banks returned to lending after several days due to the improvement in liquidity.
One-week money was at 7.30/40 percent against 7.80/85, two-week at 7.30/40 against 7.70/80 and one-month at 7.25/30 against 7.35/38.
Three-month money was quoted at 7.25/30 percent against 7.35/40 and six-month at 7.30/35 against 7.35/40.
Dealers said the matured amount, which was raised as part of Bank Negara's open market operations, must have been large to have had such an impact on the market.
Bank Negara regularly intervenes in the money market to keep liquidity under check and set interest rates. It does not reveal the amount it borrows from the market.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mostly higher in tandem with the rising interbank rates, futures dealers said.
They said local buying returned to boost the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) contracts.
The spot month December contract was unchanged at 92.81, or an implied yield of 7.19 percent.
The 1997 contracts were all higher. March was up four at 92.94, June rose five to 93.05, September was seven points higher at 93.07 and December gained three to 93.08.
"Some institutions have been buying despite the declines last week. They continue buying today because they perceive interest rates coming down next year," a futures dealer said.
